records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
Heavy snowfall expected Sunday.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 10 to 20 cm.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Beginning Sunday morning and ending Sunday evening.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking northeast across the region will bring heavy snow. A snowfall warning may be issued as the event approaches. 

Allow extra time for travel. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

records.headline: Blizzard warning
records.description:
Blizzard in Clyde River for Saturday.

Falling snow and strong northwest winds of 60 gusting up to 80 km/h has yielded to  blizzard conditions in Clyde River for Saturday. Blizzard conditions will improve Saturday late evening or overnight has winds gradually become lighter.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

records.area: Coastal waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee FL out 20 NM
records.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 10:29AM EST until November 21 at 11:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
records.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee FL out 20 NM...

* Until 1100 AM EST.

* At 1029 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over Shark Point, moving east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to nearly 50 knots, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Shark Point, Whitewater Bay, and Northwest Cape Sable.
records.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

records.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 10:21AM EST until November 21 at 11:15AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
records.description:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
All Southeast Georgia coastal waters from Altamaha Sound GA to
Fernandina Beach FL out to 60 NM...

* At 1021 AM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line from 27 NM east of St Simons

moving northwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...

20 NM and Waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Fernandina Beach FL from

overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor

records.area: Monroe Upper Keys; Monroe Middle Keys; Monroe Lower Keys
records.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 21 at 10:16AM EST until November 22 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Key West FL
records.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...All of the Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
records.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

records.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 21 at 10:13AM EST by NWS Indianapolis IN
records.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 21 at 11:11AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
records.description:
According to the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center an earthquake
occurred about 65 miles northwest of Isla de Isla Mona at 1100 AM
AST.

Based on location and magnitude the earthquake was not sufficient
to generate a tsunami damaging to Puerto Rico and the US Virgin
Islands. Some of these areas may experience non-damaging sea
level changes.

records.area: Coastal Nassau; Northeast Coastal St. Johns; Southeast Coastal St. Johns
records.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 21 at 9:33AM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
8 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Nassau, Northeast Coastal St. Johns and
Southeast Coastal St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
records.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

records.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 21 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Pittsburgh PA
records.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Saturday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

records.area: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
records.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 9:27AM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
records.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo.

* WHEN...Through 6 PM AST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
records.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:24AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through mid next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

records.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 21 at 5:05AM MST until November 21 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
records.description:

I-84 corridor this morning. Additional snow accumulations of 1 to 2
inches expected.

* WHERE...Wasatch Mountains I-80 North.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.
records.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. For winter road conditions from the
Utah Department of Transportation, visit
http://www.udottraffic.utah.gov.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

For graphical depictions of the snowfall forecast, including Official
NWS Forecast, High End Amount, and Low End Amount, visit
weather.gov/slc/winter.

records.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
records.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

records.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 21 at 12:38AM EST by NWS Indianapolis IN
records.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM
EST THIS MORNING...AND AGAIN FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EST
SUNDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

records.area: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
records.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 20 at 8:34PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
records.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides and large surf may cause
moderate to major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one half to one foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon with
peak impacts occurring 2 hours before through 2 hours after
high tide along the respective coastline areas.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
records.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 8:34PM PST until November 21 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf
may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides
if storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas
in and around Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST
Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt
Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at
9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday,
11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on
Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin

records.area: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 2:52PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
records.description:
* WHAT...Up to 3.0 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday, 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday,
2.3 ft above normal (8.1 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.9 ft
above normal (8.7 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 3.0 ft above
normal (8.8 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.6 ft above
normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions
include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical
tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes
earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San
Francisco Bay, respectively.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

records.description:

issued a Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert on Saturday for the
Susquehanna Valley.

A Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for
sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, people
suffering from asthma, heart disease or other lung diseases,
and the elderly. The effects of air pollution can be minimized
by avoiding strenuous activity or exercise outdoors.

visit www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.

records.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 20 at 11:10AM EST by NWS Indianapolis IN
records.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EST SATURDAY and 6 PM SATURDAY TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

records.area: South Devon coast at Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish
records.event: Flood Warning: South Devon coast at Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish
records.headline: Flooding is expected: South Devon coast at Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish
records.description:
High tides, strong winds and large waves are expected to cause flooding tomorrow. 

Flooding is expected 3 hours either side of high tides 

Areas at risk include exposed coastal areas at Hallsands, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton, Blackpool Sands, Teignmouth Promenade and Dawlish. The high tide at Teignmouth on Sunday morning is at 04:15. Forecast total high tide level is 2.14mAOD, which is 0.56 metres above tide table level. Strong force 6 South Easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2.1m are forecast over the high tide. High tide on Sunday evening is at 16:30. Forecast total high tide level is 2.15mAOD, which is 0.4 metres above tide table level. Strong force 6 Easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2m. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   

This message will be updated by 2:00PM on Sunday 22 November or as the situation changes.
records.instruction:
Act now 
 
You should: 
- go to Check for flooding for a map of the area and to monitor up-to-date local flood information – https://check-for-flooding.service.gov.uk/target-area/113FWC2T1A2  
- act on your personal flood plan if you have one - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/personal-flood-plan 
- follow the guidance in 'What to do before or during a flood' - https://www.gov.uk/help-during-flood  
 
You can also read more about what flood warnings are – https://www.gov.uk/guidance/flood-alerts-and-warnings-what-they-are-and-what-to-do#flood-warning 
 
Stay up to date 
 
To get the latest flood information, you can: 
- go to Check for flooding 
- monitor local weather, news and travel updates 
- call Floodline on 0345 988 1188, using quickdial code 311013
records.sourceName: UK Met Office via Meteoalarm / EUMETNET

records.headline: A slow-moving band of heavy rain may cause some flooding and transport disruption, particularly across south Devon and south Cornwall.
records.description:
A band of rain will become slow-moving across southwest England during Sunday, before clearing on Sunday night. Rainfall totals of 20-40 mm are likely quite widely, with 50-70 mm over higher ground. There remains a chance of heavier and more persistent rain developing, which could bring 60-80 mm to some lower-lying areas too, particularly Torbay, South Hams and south Cornwall, and around 100 mm over Dartmoor.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
records.instruction:
Check if your property could be at risk of flooding. If so, consider preparing a flood plan and an emergency flood kit.

Give yourself the best chance of avoiding delays by checking road conditions if driving, or bus and train timetables, amending your travel plans if necessary.

People cope better with power cuts when they have prepared for them in advance. It's easy to do; consider gathering torches and batteries, a mobile phone power pack and other essential items.

Be prepared for weather warnings to change quickly: when a weather warning is issued, the Met Office recommends staying up to date with the weather forecast in your area.

records.headline: Official WARNING of GALE-FORCE GUSTS
records.description:
There is a risk of gale-force gusts (level 2 of 4).
Height range: > 1000 m; Max. gusts: ~ 75 km/h; Wind direction: west
records.instruction:
Hazard(s) caused by: single branches falling; objects flying through the air. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure free-standing objects (e.g. screens and furniture). For example, fasten tents and coverings. Watch out for falling objects outdoors (e.g. branches).

records.headline: Official WARNING of WIND GUSTS
records.description:

Max. gusts: ~ 55 km/h; Wind direction: west then north-west; Increased gusts: in exposed locations < 70 km/h
records.instruction:
Hazard(s) to expect: light objects flying through the air. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure loose objects. For example, fasten tents and coverings.
